title: Two loops for P(n)+P(n+2)
W: Replace n by P(n) + P(n + 2). Every tested start ends in 7 → 10 → 8 → 7 or in 9 → 14 → 9. Prove there are no other outcomes.
M: Prove every orbit of $n\mapsto P(n)+P(n+2)$ on $n\ge2$ enters $\{7,10,8\}$ or $\{9,14\}$.

title: Three consecutive largest factors
W: Replace n by P(n) + P(n + 1) + P(n + 2). Every tested start reaches the fixed point 14 or the loop 77 → 103 → 123 → 77. Prove it.
M: Prove every orbit of $n\mapsto P(n)+P(n+1)+P(n+2)$ on $n\ge2$ enters $\{14\}$ or $(77,103,123)$.

title: Three pairs
W: Replace n by P(n) + P(2n + 1). Every tested start ends in one of three two-step loops: 13 ↔ 16, 30 ↔ 66, 36 ↔ 76. Prove it.
M: Prove every orbit of $n\mapsto P(n)+P(2n+1)$ on $n\ge2$ enters $\{13,16\}$, $\{30,66\}$ or $\{36,76\}$.

title: Every binary block in Gerver's constant
W: Show every finite string of 0s and 1s appears somewhere in the binary expansion of Gerver's sofa area.
M: Prove the binary expansion of $\mu_G$ is disjunctive (contains every finite word).

title: An irrational sum over largest factors
W: Add 1/(n·P(n)) over all n ≥ 2. Show the total is irrational.
M: Prove $\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{1}{n\,P(n)}$ is irrational.

title: Smooth p²+1
W: Show infinitely many primes p have p² + 1 built only from primes below √p.
M: Prove infinitely many primes $p$ with $P(p^2+1)<p^{1/2}$.

title: Large prime factors of 2^n + 3^n
W: Show the largest prime factor of 2^n + 3^n grows faster than n².
M: Prove $P(2^n+3^n)/n^2\to\infty$.

title: Sidon sets of seven-free numbers
W: Find the largest subset of the seven-free numbers up to N with all pairwise sums distinct, up to a constant factor.
M: Determine the order of magnitude of $\max\{|A|:A\subseteq\{n\le N:7\notin n\},\ A\text{ Sidon}\}$.

title: Prime Nim with Pythagorean primes
W: In a variant of Prime Nim you may only remove 2 or a prime that is 1 mod 4. Show the losing positions have density zero.
M: For the subtraction game with move set $\{2\}\cup\{p\equiv1\ (4)\}$, prove the P-positions have natural density 0.

title: The Hamiltonicity game on square sums
W: Maker and Breaker alternately claim edges of the square-sum graph. Maker wants a path through every number. Show Maker wins for large N.
M: Prove Maker wins the Maker–Breaker Hamiltonicity game on $S_N$ for all sufficiently large $N$.

title: Prime Nim is not automatic
W: Show no finite automaton reading the digits of n in any base can recognise the losing positions of Prime Nim.
M: Prove $\{n:G(n)=0\}$ is not $k$-automatic for any $k\ge2$.

title: Square-sum graph spectral gap
W: Show the square-sum graph's random walk mixes in about log N steps.
M: Prove the normalized Laplacian of the giant component of $S_N$ has spectral gap $\ge c>0$ for all large $N$.

title: Infinite cube-sum paths
W: Colour the integers with two colours. Show there is an infinite one-coloured chain where neighbours sum to cubes.
M: Prove every 2-colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ admits $a_1<a_2<\cdots$ of one colour with $a_i+a_{i+1}$ a perfect cube for all $i$.

title: Erdős–Gyárfás in square sums
W: Show every subgraph of the square-sum graph where all degrees are at least 3 contains a cycle whose length is a power of two.
M: Prove every subgraph $H\subseteq S_\infty$ with $\delta(H)\ge3$ contains a cycle of length $2^k$ for some $k\ge2$.

title: Twin-prime-free sums
W: How many numbers up to N can you keep so that no two of them sum to one member of a twin-prime pair?
M: Determine $\lim_N\frac1N\max\{|A|:A\subseteq[N],\ a+a'\notin T\ \forall a\ne a'\in A\}$, where $T=\{p:p\pm2\text{ prime}\}$.

title: Stopping times of the doubling map
W: For n ↦ 2P(n) + 1, find the typical number of steps to reach its eight-number loop.
M: For $h(n)=2P(n)+1$, prove the number of steps to enter the 8-cycle is $\sim c\log\log n$ for almost all $n$ and find $c$.

title: Lattice packing of the sofa
W: Find the densest lattice packing of Gerver's sofa exactly, as a closed form in Gerver's constants.
M: Determine $\delta_L(G)$ for Gerver's sofa $G$ in closed form over $\mathbb{Q}(\text{Gerver's algebraic parameters})$, and prove the optimal lattice is unique.

title: Spectre Laplacian
W: Take the spectre tile as a drum. Show the lowest frequency is a transcendental number.
M: Let $\lambda_1$ be the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of the unit-edge spectre polygon. Prove $\lambda_1\notin\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$.

title: Blow-up rate for the forced NS singularity
W: For the recent forced Navier–Stokes blow-up, prove the exact rate at which the velocity grows near the blow-up time.
M: For the forced finite-time singularity of 3D NS, prove $\|u(t)\|_\infty\sim C(T-t)^{-1/2}$ and show the profile is asymptotically self-similar with a unique profile.

title: Periodic billiards in the hat
W: Show the hat polygon has a periodic billiard path, and that the number of them grows quadratically in length.
M: Prove $N(L)\sim cL^2$ for the number of cylinder families of periodic billiard trajectories of length $\le L$ in the hat polygon, with $c>0$.

title: Moser's worm in the sphere
W: Find the smallest area region on the unit sphere that can cover every curve of length 1 after a rotation.
M: Determine $\inf\{\sigma(K):K\subset S^2$ covers every rectifiable curve of length $1$ up to $SO(3)\}$ to within $1\%$, and prove the infimum is attained by a set bounded by finitely many circular arcs or show it is not.

title: Cheeger constant of the sofa
W: Find the Cheeger constant of Gerver's sofa and show it is transcendental.
M: Prove $h(G)=\inf_{E\subseteq G}\mathrm{Per}(E)/|E|$ for Gerver's sofa is transcendental.

title: Dimers on the hat tiling
W: Count perfect matchings of large patches of the hat tiling's dual graph and find the entropy per tile.
M: Prove the dimer entropy per tile of the hat-tiling dual graph exists and compute it in closed form, or prove it is not a period.

title: Random Prime Nim
W: Two players play Prime Nim but each move uses a random prime chosen by a coin. Find the probability the first player wins from a large pile.
M: In the game where a move $n\mapsto n-p$ must use $p$ from a random set $R\subseteq\mathbb{P}$ ($p\in R$ independently w.p. $1/2$), prove $\Pr(\text{N-position at }n)$ converges as $n\to\infty$ and determine its limit.

title: Random sequential prime-sum packing
W: Add random numbers from 1 to N one at a time, keeping a number only if it forms no prime sum with any kept number. Find the final density.
M: Determine $\lim_N\mathbb{E}|A_N|/N$ for the random sequential independent set of the prime-sum graph on $[N]$.

title: Glauber dynamics on hat tiling Potts
W: Show the 3-state Potts model on the hat tiling has a continuous phase transition at the self-dual point.
M: Prove the $q=3$ Potts model on the hat-tiling vertex graph has a continuous phase transition and that the critical point satisfies an explicit algebraic equation.

title: Sharp threshold for prime-sum Hamiltonicity
W: Keep each edge of the prime-sum graph with probability p. Find the threshold for a Hamiltonian cycle.
M: For random subgraphs of the prime-sum graph on $[2n]$ with edge probability $p$, prove the Hamiltonicity threshold is $p^*=(1+o(1))\frac{\log^2 n}{n}$ times an explicit constant, and determine it.

title: Prime factor plus digit sum
W: Add the largest prime factor of n to its digit sum. Every tested start ends in 6 → 9 → 12. Prove all do, which needs ruling out endless chains of primes p → p + digit sum.
M: For $f(n)=P(n)+s_{10}(n)$, prove every orbit with $n\ge2$ reaches the cycle $(6,9,12)$.

title: The field of Gerver's sofa
W: Gerver's sofa is described by numbers in a specific algebraic number field. Determine the degree and Galois group of the field they generate.
M: Let $K$ be the field generated over $\mathbb{Q}$ by $\cos$ and $\sin$ of Gerver's four angle parameters and the sofa area. Determine $[K:\mathbb{Q}]$, or prove $K$ is not a number field.

title: Formal verification depth of RH
W: The Riemann hypothesis now has a Lean proof. Show it cannot be proved in a weak arithmetic like I-Sigma-1 plus exponentiation, or show it can.
M: Decide whether RH (as a $\Pi^0_1$ sentence) is provable in $\mathrm{I}\Sigma_1$, or in $\mathrm{EFA}$.

title: Square subtraction with prime piles
W: In the game where you subtract a square, show infinitely many prime pile sizes are losing positions.
M: Prove infinitely many primes are P-positions of the subtract-a-square game.

title: Seven-free factorial-like products
W: Show n! + 1 contains the digit 7 for all large n.
M: Prove $7\in n!+1$ (decimal) for all sufficiently large $n$.

title: Largest prime factor of 2^n + n
W: Show the largest prime factor of 2^n + n tends to infinity faster than any fixed multiple of n.
M: Prove $P(2^n+n)/n\to\infty$.

title: Book thickness of the square-sum graph
W: Show the square-sum graph on 1 to N can be drawn with vertices on a line and edges on a bounded number of pages without crossings.
M: Prove $\sup_N\mathrm{bt}(S_N)<\infty$ for the book thickness, or that it is unbounded.
